items.title: Concerns NDIS changes could push families towards child protection services
items.description: Exhausted families could be plunged further into crisis and have greater interaction with child protection services under the proposed overhaul of the NDIS, advocates say.

items.title: Live: Coalition 'indistinguishable' from One Nation, PM says
items.description: Anthony Albanese says the Coalition is at risk of becoming "indistinguishable" from One Nation after the opposition leader did not rule out a preference deal. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Barbeques Galore to shut, hundreds of workers facing redundancy
items.description: It will shut its 62 company-owned stores in the coming weeks and working through "transitional arrangements" with 27 stores owned by franchises, with hundreds of staff facing redundancy.

items.title: Live: ASX remains in the red, NAB sees next RBA move as down
items.description: The local share market is in the red but has clawed back some ground from its early lows. Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI files to become a public company in the US. Follow live.

items.title: Outpouring of support as ex-NRL player Kane Evans comes out
items.description: Evans is the second professional rugby league player in Australian history to publicly come out, following Ian Roberts in 1995.

items.title: How the regime is sneaking tankers past Trump's blockade
items.description: Amid new strikes, the future of the Strait of Hormuz has again been plunged into uncertainty, but ships are finding a way through.

items.title: Why a property downturn would be a blessing for the RBA
items.description: With two Australian banks cutting fixed home loan rates, there is a ray of hope that the cycle of interest rate hikes has peaked and borrowing costs may be lower down the track — another sign the pace of economic change has moved into overdrive.

items.title: We were happier during the COVID-19 pandemic. The reason is money
items.description: Australians felt a greater sense of satisfaction during the COVID-19 pandemic than they do today, according to government data, when households are grappling with the impact of inflation, rising interest rates and a reduction in real wages.

items.title: Young couple told by agent that landlords would not rent to 'people like you'
items.description: Hopeful renters say negative stereotypes about young people are making it almost impossible to secure a rental on the Sunshine Coast.

items.title: Donald Trump booed at NBA Finals as chaos ensues outside
items.description: US President Donald Trump cops the vitriol of the Madison Square Garden crowd after causing chaos to attend the NBA Finals.

items.title: ABC boss confirms ex-news director in the dark about replacement hunt
items.description: Managing director Hugh Marks is questioned by Sally Sara over Justin Stevens's sudden resignation last month, in addition to controversies over the hiring of Grace Tame and subsequent comments by radio host Charlie Pickering.

items.title: The bad blood between Poland and Ukraine left over from World War II
items.description: Poland is weighing whether to strip Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of its top honour for renaming an army unit after Ukrainian nationalist insurgents who massacred Poles in World War II.

items.title: Police say 17yo fired 30 shots at wrong funeral venue for Sydney crime boss
items.description: Two people are charged over a shooting at what was advertised as the venue for a Sydney crime boss's funeral.

items.title: Seven arrested as police manhunt for escaped bikie continues
items.description: Seven people have been arrested as police continue to look for Mongols bikie Brandt Graham who escaped from custody last week.

items.title: Idris Elba thinks audiences won't support a black James Bond
items.description: Idris Elba has quashed rumours he was ever in the running to play James Bond, saying audiences are unlikely to come along for the ride if Bond is played by a black actor.

items.title: The criticism Marc Fennell always gets for Stuff the British Stole
items.description: Two years in the making, the Walkley Award-winning journalist is back with the third season of his globe-trotting historical mystery series. He's treating it like it's the last.

items.title: From the Kimberley to Sweden, how heartbreak helped me take a travel leap
items.description: As I approached the age of 30, I longed to travel outside of Australia, but there was always an excuse or obstacle. A chance to share my culture with the world finally got me there.

items.title: Escaped devil spotted on suburban Gold Coast CCTV after week on loose
items.description: A two-year-old Tasmanian devil has been on the loose since last Tuesday when she leapt out of her enclosure at a Gold Coast wildlife park.

items.title: 'I'm all in': Jacinta Allan brushes off leadership rumblings
items.description: The Victorian premier said she had no plans to step aside despite some Labor MPs becoming increasingly frustrated by her performance as leader and more worrying opinion polls.

items.title: Breaking: Damning report finds WA prisoners subjected to 'cruel, degrading treatment'
items.description: WA prisoners are being subjected to "cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment" because the state government has allowed prisons to become "almost fundamentally broken", according to the Inspector of Custodial Services.

items.title: Woman accused of murdering terminally ill partner granted bail
items.description: The judge said new evidence showed the Kylie Truswell Mobbs's husband David Mobbs, who had motor neurone disease, was "resolute" in his desire to die.

items.title: Former WA Police officer 'gutted' after compensation for horrific injury denied
items.description: Former WA Police officer and WA Australian of the Year Paul Litherland says he is "heartbroken" after his claim for post-service medical compensation over injuries he received in the force was denied.

items.title: Family's 'worst nightmare' after purchasing home filled with defects
items.description: After a young family invests their life savings in their dream home, only to discover it is filled with defects, SA's consumer watchdog issues a public warning notice about the builder responsible and seven other traders.

items.title: Residents shocked by severe storm as South West WA homes left flooded
items.description: An unexpected deluge has flooded homes and public facilities in the South West WA town of Harvey. The community was pelted with 40mm of rain in one hour.

items.title: 'Violence brokers' are transforming organised crime in Sydney
items.description: One of the state's top police officers has promised feuding gangs bringing terror to Sydney's streets will not exist "by the time we finish" as police stare down a new era of disorganised crime.
